subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept default-off model-mediated writes to SOUL.md in core, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces instead?
rationale: The requested behavior is missing and well scoped, but it writes user/model-derived text into a prompt-loaded instruction file and adds new config, CLI, and tool surfaces.

options.title: Accept guarded core contract
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only if it preserves private `soul_update` gating, explicit opt-in, provenance, escaping, notice, undo, and hostile-input coverage.

options.title: Move to memory or plugin seam
options.body: Reject direct SOUL.md mutation in core and ask for durable preference capture through memory plugins or a new plugin/API extension.

options.title: Decline automatic mutation
options.body: Close the SOUL auto-evolution direction if maintainers do not want any model-mediated instruction-file writes.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only if it preserves private `soul_update` gating, explicit opt-in, provenance, escaping, notice, undo, and hostile-input coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans SOUL docs, prompt assembly, plugin boundaries, and security posture, where the history points to this owner as a strong routing candidate.
